title: Chapter 2 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of disabilities and assistive technologies.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a situational disability?
options: Using a phone in bright sunlight
questions.explanation: Situational disabilities arise from context, not a medical condition.

questions.question: What technology is primarily used by blind users to browse the web?
questions.explanation: Screen readers convert digital content into speech or braille output.

questions.question: Colour should never be used to convey information because colour blind users can't see any colours.
questions.explanation: Colour can be used, but it must not be the *only* way to convey information.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a screen reader's navigation shortcut?
options: Press H to jump to the next help section
Press H to jump to the next heading
questions.explanation: H jumps to the next heading, allowing rapid skimming of page structure.

questions.question: A person with a broken arm is considered to have a _____ disability.
questions.explanation: Temporary disabilities result from injury or illness that will heal.

questions.question: The _____ is a structured representation of a page that assistive technologies use.
questions.explanation: The accessibility tree is built from the DOM and provides semantic meaning.

questions.question: What is the recommended minimum target size for interactive elements according to WCAG 2.5.5?
questions.explanation: 44 by 44 CSS pixels ensures sufficient area for touch and click activation.

questions.question: Auto-generated captions are fully accessible for deaf users.
questions.explanation: Auto captions often lack accuracy, punctuation, and speaker identification; they must be reviewed.

questions.question: What does a switch device typically do?
options: Emulates a single keyboard input or mouse click
questions.explanation: A switch is a simple binary device used with scanning software to interact with the UI.

questions.question: Which group represents the largest number of people with disabilities on the web?
questions.explanation: Cognitive disabilities are the most common, including dyslexia, ADHD, and memory issues.

questions.question: Why is it important to provide text alternatives for audio alerts?
options: For screen reader users who are blind
For deaf or hard of hearing users
questions.explanation: Visual alternatives help deaf users, while screen reader users also benefit from text announcements.

questions.question: What is audio description primarily used for?
questions.explanation: Audio description narrates visual elements for people who are blind or have low vision.

questions.question: People with motor disabilities never use a screen reader.
questions.explanation: Some motor‑impaired users who cannot use a keyboard may combine voice control with a screen reader.

questions.question: What does 'prefers-reduced-motion' in CSS help with?
options: Removing animations for users who are prone to seizures or distraction
questions.explanation: It respects users' system settings to reduce or eliminate non‑essential motion, aiding those with vestibular disorders or ADHD.

questions.question: Which of the following is a best practice for cognitive accessibility?
options: Making users guess what a button does
questions.explanation: Consistency reduces cognitive load and helps users build a mental model.

questions.question: The 'curb‑cut effect' describes how accessibility features end up helping _____.
questions.explanation: Features designed for disabilities often benefit a much wider audience.

questions.question: What is the first step a screen reader user often takes to understand a new page?
options: Read every word from top to bottom
questions.explanation: Screen reader users frequently jump from heading to heading to get an outline of the content.

questions.question: A website can be fully accessible without being keyboard accessible.
questions.explanation: Keyboard accessibility is a fundamental requirement; many assistive technologies depend on keyboard‑like input.

questions.question: Which disability type might benefit from a 'skip to main content' link?
questions.explanation: Skip links allow keyboard users to bypass repetitive navigation, which is especially important for motor disabilities.

questions.question: Voice control software relies heavily on what HTML property to target elements?
questions.explanation: Voice control uses the accessible name (from label, aria‑label, or text content) to identify elements.
